King Sun (born Todd Ramakhan Turnbow; February 23, 1967) is an American rapper and songwriter known for melding Five-Percent Nation teachings, Afrocentric themes, and street-oriented lyricism during hip-hop’s golden era. He is considered one of the earliest hip-hop artists to openly incorporate Five-Percenter ideology into mainstream music.
Early life
King Sun was born in Paterson, New Jersey and raised in both Paterson and the Bronx, New York. He was raised under the teachings of the Nation of Islam (NOI) during the 1970s. In 1980, he was introduced to the Five-Percent Nation. After spending time at Jamesburg Youth Prison in New Jersey, he fully embraced Five-Percenter teachings upon release.
In 1986, King Sun attended a Rakim performance at a bar in Paterson. After joining a freestyle with Rakim, he was discovered by Robert Hill, founder of Zakia Records, who signed him to a recording contract.
Career
He made his debut in 1987 with the single "Hey Love" with producer D-Moet, which peaked at #69 on the US Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. Turnbow signed to Zakia Records and Profile Records that same year.
XL (1989)
King Sun’s debut album, XL, was released in 1989 on Zakia/Profile Records. The album featured the single "Hey Love" (1987) and the B-side "Mythological Rapper", along with "On the Club Tip" and "It’s a Heat Up". His music blended Afrocentric themes with street narratives, rooted in the philosophy of the Five-Percent Nation.
Righteous but Ruthless (1990)
In 1990, King Sun released his second album, Righteous but Ruthless, on Profile Records. The album included the socially conscious anthem "Be Black" (1990), "Undercover Lover", and "Big Shots". It achieved moderate commercial success and critical respect in hip-hop circles.
Strictly Ghetto (1994)
His third studio release, Strictly Ghetto, came out in 1994 under Cold Chillin'/Warner Bros. It featured a grittier sound that reflected the changing landscape of hip-hop in the mid-1990s.
Legacy
Although King Sun never achieved mainstream superstardom, he is considered a pioneer of conscious hip-hop. His work laid the groundwork for artists such as Rakim, Brand Nubian, Poor Righteous Teachers, and members of the Wu-Tang Clan. He remains respected for his lyrical depth and cultural impact.
